title: Prompt weights: what the brackets really do

questions.q: What weight does brass get in ((brass:1.3))?
questions.why: A number replaces the weight outright. The 1.1 multiplies are thrown away.

options: The arrow from the empty prompt's row to this token's row
questions.answer: The arrow from the empty prompt's row to this token's row

questions.q: What does weight 0 do to the token?
options: Puts its row where the empty prompt's row is at that position, keeping the length
Removes it from the tokens before encoding
questions.answer: Puts its row where the empty prompt's row is at that position, keeping the length
questions.why: Formula with weight 0 gives z_empty[j]. The tensor isn't shortened.

questions.q: Why does a weight not reach other tokens through the encoder?
options: It is applied after the encoder has run
questions.answer: It is applied after the encoder has run
questions.why: encode_token_weights encodes first, then changes rows.

questions.q: You use (brass:1.5) on FLUX.2 Klein. What happens?
options: No weight applies: the tokenizer passes disable_weights=True
questions.answer: No weight applies: the tokenizer passes disable_weights=True
questions.why: KleinTokenizer calls the base tokenizer with disable_weights=True.
